items.title: hover and go-to-definition answer NOTHING on a call whose argument is a closure carrying a `context` clause — `m.switch_some(\|v\| ..)`, `n.switch(\|v\| ..)`, `and_then` — blanket or not: the analysis leaves no entity record (`entity_map`, `function_calls`) for the call, only its span
items.body: Probe on editor-46 (fe092e8d + lane): `fun pick(m: MemoCell<Option<i32>>, n: MemoCell<i32>) { let _ = m.switch_some(|value| MemoCell::new(value)); let _ = n.distinct(); let _ = n.switch(|value| MemoCell::new(value)); }` — hover on `distinct` answers (`impl type F: Flow<type T: PartialEq>` …), hover on `switch_some` and `switch` answers `None`. The call's id has a span in `span_map` but no `entity_map` entry and no `function_calls` record; the parameter type `(sync |T| I) context (owner_scope, tracking, ambient_nursery)` suggests the context pass's lowering replaces the call record without keeping the source subject (E72/E75's `source_call_subject` cannot reach it). The editor cannot resolve what the program no longer says. Rec: keep the call's record (or an erased-subject entry, as `context_erased_subjects` does for `get_safe`) through the lowering. analyzer.rs / context.rs. Sizing S–M.

items.title: M104 leaves a file holding platform-fenced TWINS on its own analysis: serve each twin leg from the world of the entry whose platform admits it
items.body: Entry-world analysis serves a module from its primary entry's world, and a module both platforms reach reports the other entry's world's diagnostics too. A file with platform-fenced twins keeps F27 R3's kept legs (one whole analysis per platform, the file as its own entry), so it pays its own worlds and shows module-local diagnostics, unlike its neighbours. Build: the primary leg is a view of the primary entry's world, each kept twin leg a view of the entry whose platform admits that twin (`TwinLeg { document: Document::view_of(..) }`), and a twin no entry's platform admits keeps today's leg. kolt carries no twins. Sizing M.

items.title: `let x: i32 = 2 * true;` checks clean and the JS build prints `2` — an integer multiplied by a `bool` is accepted
items.body: Repro on v0.43.0 (installed toolchain): a package whose `server.vl` is `fun main() { let x: i32 = 2 * true; print(x); }` — `vilan check .` reports nothing, `vilan run .` prints 2 (JS coerces `true` to 1). `model.count * true` inside a function body was equally clean. Expected: `i32: Mul<bool>` has no impl — the operator refusal every other mismatched operand gets. Native untested. Sizing S–M.
